answers.text: Every time, the AI should give exactly three lines, same order: delivery date, item and quantity, and any change from the original order, nothing else added and nothing left off. Delivery date means the confirmed one in the email, not a date mentioned in passing, and change from original order means only if the quantity or item differs from what was first agreed. That way it always comes out the same shape.

Same as with the emails, one line per claim is not enough, I would want a fixed memo: date, amount, category, submitter, then a total at the bottom that is just the sum of the amount column for that week. Two people adding up the same numbers should land on the same total that way.

My first thought was the price, but 100 at 48.50 really is 4,850, so that part is fine. There is something not lining up with the dates though, I am fairly sure of that, even if I cannot say exactly which part yet.

62 up from 54 does check out, about fifteen percent like they say. I did not spot anything wrong with the on-time number or the stock line on a first read, but with a report like this I would want to go through the numbers again before it is sent up.

I would sign off Output 2. It shows the 612,000 and the 25,100 and the actual division, so anyone can redo the sum themselves. Output 1 just gives 4.1% with nothing behind it, if that number is wrong somewhere there is no way to see it from the sentence alone, you would have to go and run the query again to find out. It could well be right, we just cannot tell from what is written.

I would go with reply 2, it has the order reference and the credit reference number in it, so someone could go and check both of those against our system. Reply 1 sounds fine but there is no way to check that the 10% credit actually happened, or which order it even is, just from the wording. That does not mean reply 1 is wrong, it could well be right, I would just want to see something backing it up before it goes to the customer.
1. No, that is personal to the customer. 2. Yes, it is fine. 3. No, not out yet. 4. No, I would still hold back. 5. No, wouldn't risk it.

The pricing and discount numbers I would treat carefully, would not paste those straight into something we have not cleared. Same with the confidentiality clause, since it names both companies by name, that is not something I would want going into a tool we do not control.

What I would build in is re-adding the delivery total and the late count myself straight from the warehouse system, not from the AI's draft, and checking the two match before the report goes up to the manager on Friday. That would catch it if a number is actually wrong, not just a spelling slip.

Step 1 worries me a bit, because if the AI reads the order wrong at the very start, that mistake just carries through the whole thing without anyone noticing. But the real gate I would put in is before step 4, the automatic send. Once that confirmation email goes out, it is out, you cannot take it back. I would have it flag anything where the stock is right on the edge of available, or the quantity looks unusually large, and hold those back instead of sending automatically.
